name: Propranolol
metabolism: Extensive first-pass metabolism includes CYP2D6 aromatic hydroxylation, side-chain processing and direct glucuronidation. CYP2C19 also participates. Most metabolites are eliminated in urine.
summary: Propranolol is a non-selective beta blocker used to treat high blood pressure, some heart rhythm disorders, performance anxiety, and other conditions, and to help prevent migraine and further heart problems.
toxicities: Label-reported adverse reactions include bradycardia, hypotension, heart failure, dizziness/light-headedness, fatigue, and mental depression.
Overdose can cause hypotension and bradycardia; serious cardiac depression may require emergency supportive treatment.

Other serious risks include bronchospasm, hypoglycemia (which may be harder to recognize), worsening heart failure, and ischemia or myocardial infarction after abrupt discontinuation in at-risk patients.
generalRisks: The label contraindicates propranolol in cardiogenic shock, sinus bradycardia or greater-than-first-degree heart block, bronchial asthma, and hypersensitivity. Of hypotension/bradycardia and cardiac failure, bronchospasm, hypoglycemia with masked warning signs, and worsening angina or myocardial infarction after abrupt discontinuation. Overdose can produce hypotension and bradycardia.
saferUse: Do not use with asthma, marked bradycardia, significant heart block, or cardiogenic shock; use requires clinical assessment.
Overdose can dangerously slow heart rate and lower blood pressure; seek emergency care for suspected excess or fainting, severe weakness, breathing difficulty, or collapse.
Do not stop long-term therapy abruptly; the label advises gradual reduction over several weeks. Alcohol and interacting cardiovascular or metabolism-affecting medicines may alter effects or exposure.
dosageRemark: The label provides prescription regimens for cardiovascular indications, migraine prevention, and essential tremor. These are not recreational dose guidance; recreational thresholds and duration are not established here.
